title: MLB Logo Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The MLB Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo?
description: A hard MLB logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of MLB team logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the team, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from an MLB team logo, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No full letters, no team names. Each piece still holds one real detail, a color pair, a serif or a curve that only one club owns.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

readMore.label: How Every MLB Team Got Its Colors

items.piece: The gold outline running across the navy glove.
items.fact: The ball-in-glove logo hides an m and a b for Milwaukee Brewers. Tom Meindel, an art student at UW-Eau Claire, drew it for a 1977 team contest. It debuted in 1978 and came back as the main logo in 2020.

items.piece: The points of the compass star.
items.fact: The compass star has been at the center of the Mariners' logo since the team's 1993 redesign.

items.piece: The inside corner of the T, with its blue shadow.
items.fact: The Rangers began as the second Washington Senators and moved to Texas in 1972.

items.piece: The pinched waist of the B.
items.fact: Boston took the Red Sox name in 1908, borrowing the red stockings the city's earlier National League club had dropped.

items.piece: The blue ring meeting the top of the red C.
items.fact: The Cubs have played at Wrigley Field since 1916, and the red C inside the blue ring is one of the most recognizable marks in baseball.

items.piece: The top of the script A.
items.fact: The franchise dates to 1871 in Boston and moved to Milwaukee in 1953 and Atlanta in 1966.

items.piece: The foot of the A in LA.
items.fact: The name goes back to Brooklyn, where fans were called Trolley Dodgers for dodging the streetcars that crossed the borough.

items.piece: The point where the N and the Y cross.
items.fact: The interlocking NY was designed by Tiffany & Co. in 1877 for a New York City police medal, decades before the Yankees used it.
